newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian PM maintains confidence in his deputy.
newsitem.headline: Belgian PM maintains confidence in his deputy.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Thursday he retained confidence in Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo who is at the centre of a scandal over allegations he had sex with young boys.

Dehaene was in parliament to answer questions after parliament decided earlier on Thursday to follow a recommendation by a commission of its members that further investigation into the allegations, hotly denied by Di Rupo, was needed.

"In view of the state of the judicial procedure it would be premature at this stage to take a political decision and (Di Rupo) retains my confidence," Dehaene said in his first public comment on the affair.

Di Rupo had told Dehaene personally that he deplored the way the allegations had been aired and he denied all of them. "He confirmed to me that he could continue to carry out fully his ministerial functions," Dehaene said.

"For the minister, political leaders, the system of political democracy, and the sense of justice of the whole population, it is of the utmost importance to clarify this case as soon as possible," Dehaene said.

For the opposition VLD liberal party, Patrick Dewael said "the VLD believes that Deputy Prime Minister Di Rupo has to step down...because he no longer has the political integrity and moral authority required of a deputy prime minister."
